issues: Minor scope/wording overreach risk: the mitigation list and “banking book” phrasing may be read as broader, controlled frameworks than evidenced (risk register entries and scenario methodology are the only support).
Deterministic warning on strong language (“validated”): even though framed as target-record attributes, the executive summary should further reduce assurance/verification ambiguity.

Some high-salience scenario outputs and assumption ranges available in the evidence package are not included, reducing decision-usefulness (stranded assets estimate; revenue-at-risk; key assumption ranges).
available_evidence_omitted: Scenario-analysis quantitative highlights available in the evidence package but not mentioned: max stranded assets estimate EUR 33,575.2m (SCN0003, Net Zero 2050, 2050) and max revenue-at-risk EUR 35,509.1m (SCN0013, NDC, 2025).
Scenario assumption range disclosure available in the evidence package but not summarised: carbon price range EUR 1.2–287.1/tCO2e; technology readiness levels; temperature outcome range 1.5–3.0°C.
unsupported_claims: “The disclosures focus on the bank’s lending and banking book activities … including green finance and climate-focused capital and operating expenditure.” Evidence supports lending book and green loans/capex/opex metrics, but “banking book activities” scope is not explicitly evidenced (only lending book is clearly referenced in scenario methodology).

“Mitigation actions include … collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlays … [and] flood mapping overlays” is only evidenced as “Collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlay” for the stranded assets risk (RISK-BANK01-2024-0005); the executive summary wording can be read as broader application across multiple risks without specifying it is risk-register entry-specific.

Use of the term “validated” is flagged by deterministic pre-checks as potentially over-strong. While the executive summary mostly avoids assurance language, it references “third_party_validated flags” in a way that could still be misread as external assurance unless explicitly framed as a source-data attribute only.
